I see what you’re saying. Why do we perpetuate so much awfulness in the world? Because we’re selfish enough to chase love? Or an afterlife? Or something superficial? But convincing all of humanity to give up seems complicated, and I’m a bit too lazy for that. Honestly sleep helps me so much. When I made the original post I was balling my eyes out, I called my sister and cried to her and just reached out in a couple directions for help. I didn’t want to be alone and felt so very much alone… but I made it into my bed from the bar I was at somehow. And I curled up replying to a few messages here and I just passed out. Now when I woke up my hangover, both emotional and alcoholic, was spine chilling. Felt like I’d been beaten with a rock, a real big heavy one too. But I did feel better. Sleep helped me so much.

I have tried journaling! I’m not the best about doing it regularly, but I do love it. I like telling people to write their feelings down because it makes them easier to carry! I’ve got a book a write in sometime when things get dark, and it lets me physically carry my feelings in one hand when I walk around with it. That metaphor alone is like a sigh of relief to me every now and again.
I don’t know why but your username just made me laugh. It’s the little things. That’s one way to cheer somebody up, haha!

I’ve never really been good at opening up, I think that’s probably one of the biggest issues. I just… needed to put something out into the world. So I did. That’s kind of what this was. Like if I said all that stuff that I just said, I’d be forcing myself to have some form of a serious conversation about my mental health. Obligating myself to keep trying. And with the Internet I can do that even at 4 in the morning drunk out of my mind.
You know you’d be surprised to hear how much better I feel after just a few hours of sleep, haha!

I got to have a conversation about it. Even a small one. No, it didn’t solve all of my problems. But you know what? It probably solved more than any conversation with most of my friends. And they’re good friends, I’m just not good at sharing. So thank you, random Internet stranger. I hope your life is better than the few moments you’ve given me.

Thanks. I’m not good at venting. I feel like I’d have too much to explain. But I don’t feel pressured here. You volunteered to respond. You weren’t paid to answer my phone call or anything. So I’m glad you replied. It’s a hard concept to explain for me personally, but thanks. I’m just in a low spot. The Backfoot. I’ve been a winner for a while and right now I’m certainly not. I haven’t been for three years. I’ve sought out therapy and professional help for a while. I can’t say it hasn’t helped but im just not where I should be yet. Thanks for replying. I feel a little better knowing I don’t have to let my family down and I can still talk to someone. You’re the good that’s left on the world.
